parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “not, without”), from Proto-Hellenic *ə- (“un-, not; without, lacking”), from Proto-Indo-European *n̥- (“not, un-”). Doublet of u-. Compare an- (ἀν- (an-) immediately preceding a vowel).

parole.significato: actinium (a radioactive, metallic chemical element (symbol: Ac) with an atomic number of 89; found in uranium ores)
parole.testo: First part actin- from Ancient Greek ἀκτίς (aktís, “ray, beam”), from Proto-Hellenic [Term?], from Proto-Indo-European *nókʷ-t-u-s ~ *n̥kʷ-t-éw-s, from *nókʷts (“night”), from *negʷ- (“bare, naked”). Last part from Latin -ium (forms names of chemical elements), from -ius (forms adjectives).
From Ancient Greek ἄκρος (ákros, “topmost, outmost, inmost; highest”).

parole.significato: a short saying or utterance, especially one attributed to Jesus and treated as a distinct textual unit
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek λόγιον (lógion, “announcement, oracle; divine utterance”), from λόγος (lógos, “word, saying”), from Proto-Hellenic *lógos, from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to collect (words)”). Compare Swedish logion, German Logion and English logion.
